name: Wandsworth

licensing.selective: Selective licensing covers Furzedown, South Balham, Tooting Bec and Tooting Broadway (designation 1, from 1 July 2025) and East Putney, West Putney and Northcote (designation 2, from 1 April 2026 until 31 March 2031), for privately rented homes that aren't HMOs.
licensing.additional: Additional licensing covers the whole borough from 1 July 2025 for HMOs not covered by mandatory licensing, including smaller shared homes and flats in multiple occupation in purpose-built blocks of three or more flats.
licensing.fee: Selective licence £850 per property; additional HMO licence £1,450 per property, each paid in two parts (Part A on application, Part B when granted).

housing: Wandsworth has one of the largest private rented sectors in London (36.3% of households in 2021), popular with young professionals sharing Victorian and Edwardian terraces in Clapham Junction, Balham, Tooting and Earlsfield. Many terraces and mansion blocks are split into flats. Nine Elms and the Battersea Power Station area have added thousands of new high-rise flats, while Roehampton’s Alton Estate and other post-war estates are under regeneration. The council’s Band D charge is one of the lowest in the country.
checkinTips: Sharer lets in Victorian terraces: photograph each bedroom, its door lock and furniture, and the shared kitchen, bathroom and garden.
Mansion block flats in Battersea, Balham and Putney: photograph the communal entrance, lift, stairs and any porter arrangements, and record every key.
New towers at Nine Elms and Battersea Power Station: photograph integrated appliances, ventilation units, glazing and balcony doors, and record fobs and parking remotes.
Sash and bay windows: photograph cords, catches, locks and any condensation or rot.
Riverside flats in Wandsworth Town and Putney: photograph balconies and any signs of damp, and note bike store and parking access.
Converted flats often share meters or have them in a communal cupboard: photograph each meter with its serial number and reading.
tenantHelp: Wandsworth Council’s private sector housing service can inspect privately rented homes for disrepair and hazards; tenants can contact it through the council’s housing pages.
